stem: What is the border line between India and China called?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The McMahon Line demarcates the northeastern boundary between India and China. This boundary line was determined in the year 1914 by Sir Henry McMahon.

stem: Which states of India have common borders with Myanmar?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram are the Indian states whose boundaries adjoin Myanmar.

stem: Which of the following countries has the longest border with India?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: India shares its longest international border with Bangladesh, with a total length of 4096.70 km. Assam, West Bengal, Mizoram, Meghalaya, and Tripura are the Indian states that share a border with Bangladesh.

stem: How many states of India have common borders with Pakistan and Bangladesh?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Indian states and Union Territories bordering Pakistan are Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Punjab, Rajasthan, and Gujarat. The Indian states bordering Bangladesh are Assam, West Bengal, Mizoram, Meghalaya, and Tripura. Therefore, no Indian state shares a common border with both Pakistan and Bangladesh.

stem:
Consider the following statements and identify the correct ones:
I. The Greater Himalayas are known for their continuity.
II. The Lesser Himalayas are known for their breadth and transverse valleys.
III. The Shiwaliks are the outer Himalayas and are the most recent in origin.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Greater Himalaya is known for its continuity from west to east. The Shiwaliks are the Outer Himalaya and are the most recent in origin. Therefore, statements I and III are correct, while statement II is incorrect.

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the formation of landforms in India :
I. Structurally, the Meghalaya Plateau is an extended part of the deccan Plateau.
II. The valley of Kashmir was formed in a synclinorium.
III. The Gangetic plain was formed in a foredeep.
Iv. The Himalayas originated as a result of triangular convergence of the Indian Plate, the European Plate and the Chinese Plate.
Which of these statements are correct?
expl: The Meghalaya Plateau is an outlier extension of the Peninsular Plateau and became separated from the main peninsula due to faulting. Structurally, it represents an extension of the Deccan Plateau. Hence, statement I is correct. The Kashmir Valley was formed in a synclinal structure of the Himalayas; therefore, statement II is correct. The Ganga Plain developed in a foredeep formed in front of the rising Himalayas and was gradually filled by alluvial deposits brought by rivers. Hence, statement III is correct. The Himalayas originated due to the collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate, not due to any triangular convergence. Therefore, statement (IV) is incorrect. Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

stem:

stem: The Indian subcontinent was originally a part of which of the following in the east?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to the theories of continental drift and plate tectonics, the Indian subcontinent was part of a vast landmass called Gondwanaland. During the period from the Jurassic to the Cretaceous, this supercontinent broke up into India, South America, Africa, Australia, and Antarctica.

stem: Southern Peninsular Highlands is a part of ______.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Southern Peninsular Highlands are a part of Gondwanaland. It mainly includes parts of Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Maharashtra, etc.

stem: The foothills region of Himalayas is –
expl: The foothill region of the Himalayas lies in the Shivalik Range. These are the southernmost ranges of the Himalayas. Many structured vallley lies between the northern slopes of the Shivaliks range and the southern slopes of the Lesser Himalayas.

stem:
Arrange the following ranges from north to South in sequence :
1. Ladakh 2. Karakoram
3. Pir Panjal 4. Zanskar
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The correct order from north to south of the Ladakh, Karakoram, Pir Panjal, and Zanskar ranges is—Karakoram, Ladakh, Zanskar, and Pir Panjal.

stem: Shivalik series was formed in –
expl: The Shivaliks, or the Outer Himalayas, were formed in the Cenozoic Era, mainly during the Miocene Pliocene epoch of the Neogene period, about 5.33–2.58 million years ago.

stem: Someshwar Range is a part of which of the following mountain ranges?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / more than one of the above

expl: Someshwar Range is a part of the Shivalik Range, i.e., the Outer Sub-Himalaya. It is noteworthy that, on the basis of age of formation and intensity of folding, the Himalayas can be divided into three parallel structural zones— (i) Greater Himalaya (Great Himalaya) (ii) Lesser Himalaya (Middle Himalaya) (iii) Outer Sub-Himalaya (Shivalik)

stem: The share of mountains in India’s total land area is—

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In India’s total land area, the share of mountains is about 29–30 percent (of the total land area). The plateau region is about 28 percent and the plain region is about 43 percent.

stem: The eastern end of the Greater Himalayas, that is, Himadri, is-
expl: Namcha Barwa is a mountain in the Himalayan range located in south-eastern Tibet. It lies at the easternmost end of the Himalayas and is the world’s 28th highest peak.

stem: Atal Tunnel is across which one of the following Himalayan ranges?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The 9.02 km long Atal Tunnel has been constructed in Himachal Pradesh on the Leh–Manali Highway in the Eastern Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas. The Atal Tunnel has been built to ensure all-weather road connectivity to the strategically important Ladakh, up to the remote Lahaul and Spiti valley. However, the tunnel will provide connectivity only up to Darcha, north of Keylong in the Lahaul region. It has been constructed under the Border Roads Organisation and is strategically important for India. In 2002, the Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Lt. Gen. Prakash Suri (Director General, Border Roads) initiated this tunnel. On 3 October 2020, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Atal Tunnel at Rohtang (Himachal Pradesh).

expl: Zoji-La Tunnel is an under-construction tunnel between Drass in Kargil district of the Union Territory of Ladakh and Sonamarg in Ganderbal district of Jammu and Kashmir. This tunnel will provide all-weather road connectivity between Srinagar (Kashmir Valley) and Leh (Ladakh).

stem: Which of the following mountain ranges divides the Ganga Plain and the deccan Plateau?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Vindhya Range is bounded by the Central Highlands in the south and the Aravalli Range in the north-west. This range divides the Ganga Plain and the Deccan Plateau.

stem: The Hills situated closer to Kanyakumari are :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Western Ghats are India’s third longest mountain range after the Himalayas. Its length is about 1600 km. It is also known as Sahyadri. The Nilgiri Hills are a knot-like elevated region where the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats meet. The highest peak of the Nilgiris is Doddabetta. The highest peak of South India, Anamudi, lies in the Anaimalai range, which is south of the Nilgiris. South of Anaimalai are the Cardamom (Elaichi) Hills. Hence, the Cardamom Hills are adjacent to Kanyakumari.

stem: Anaimalai, Cardamom Hills and Palani Hills meet at-
expl: Anamudi is the meeting point of three hill systems. To the south are the Cardamom Hills, to the north are the Anaimalai Hills, and to the north-east are the Palani Hills.

stem: At which of the following hills do the Eastern Ghats join the Western Ghats?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Nilgiri Hills are situated at the meeting point of the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats. The Nilgiri Hills are also known as the Blue Mountains. Their highest peak is Doddabetta (approximately 2637 metres high)

stem: Where the Eastern Ghats and Western Ghats meet, which of the following hills are located?
expl: The Nilgiri Hills are situated at the meeting point of the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats. The Nilgiri Hills are also known as the Blue Mountains. Their highest peak is Doddabetta (approximately 2637 metres high)

stem: Indian Oceanographers discovered a high mountain with a height of 1505 metres at the bottom of the Arabian sea about 455 km west south-west from Bombay, the mountain is called-
expl: Indian Oceanographers discovered three seamounts—one in the Central Indian Ocean Basin, another in the Eastern Arabian Sea, and the third about 455 kilometres south-west of Bombay. The seamount discovered in the Arabian Sea was named Raman Sagar Parvat (Raman Seamount) after the great scientist C. V. Raman. The other two seamounts were named after Pannikar and Wadia.

stem: Western Ghats in Maharashtra and Karnataka is known as –
expl: The Western Ghats are known as Sahyadri in Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka. Note— Nilgiri, Anaimalai and Cardamom Hills are hill ranges located within the Western Ghats.

stem: Highest mountain peak in India is–

stem: Which of the following peaks of the Himalayan mountains are not in India?
expl: Dhaulagiri peak is located in Nepal. Nanga Parbat lies in India’s Pakistan-occupied area in the Zanskar Range, while Kamet peak is located in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand.

stem: Bachendri Pal is a well-known name in the following field—
expl: Bachendri Pal, born on 24 May, 1954 in Nakuri village of Uttarkashi district (present-day Uttarakhand), is India’s first woman to climb the Mount Everest peak. Bachendri Pal hoisted the flag of victory on the summit of Everest on 23 May, 1984.

stem: The second Indian woman to climb Mount Everest was—
expl: Santosh Yadav, a resident of Haryana and an officer in the Indo-Tibetan Border Police, is the second Indian woman to achieve victory on the Mount Everest peak. Among the few women in the world to climb Everest twice, Santosh Yadav climbed Everest first in May, 1992 and again in May, 1993. For this achievement, the Government of India honoured her with the Padma Shri award in the year 2000.

stem: The snow-line in the Himalayas lies between
expl: The average height of the snow line is found at 5500–6000 m in the northern part of the Great Himalaya and at 4500– 6000 m in the southern part of the Great Himalaya. Similarly, the average snow line is found at 5800 m in the Western Himalaya and at 4300 m in the Eastern Himalaya. Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.

stem: Which of the following is the longest glacier of the Himalayan Mountains?
expl: Among the given options, Batura Glacier (57 kilometres) is the longest glacier of the Himalayas. It is located in the Karakoram Range in Pakistan-occupied Gilgit-Baltistan.

stem: Which of the following regions has the lowest snow line?

options.label: d

expl: Snow line means the altitude limit above which permanent snow remains throughout the year; due to this, generally vegetation does not grow there. Among the given options, the snow line is lowest in the Alps region.
